title: Added one Deep Learning Course
body:
Hello, cs-video-courses Contributor Team!

I've found an immeasurably valuable Deep Learning Course recently. It covers CV, NLP, RL, Multimodal topics in Deep Learning and has over 500 videos!
They are dense, math-filled and are sequenced in order of historical occurrence of described concepts, models - which is also useful. As this not only gives you a necessary theoretical background for deep-diving into more complex DL models, but also gives you a historical understanding of how AI industry developed through years.

I find it necessary to add this entry to your list - hence this PR. 
Thank you for reading this message! I will be happy to see this entry merged!

body:
Hi! This PR adds **TutorialSearch** to the *Courses* section.

### What is TutorialSearch?
[TutorialSearch](https://tutorialsearch.io/browse/ai-machine-learning/ai-video-creation) is a free, cross-platform search engine that indexes 50,000+ tutorials and courses from major learning platforms (Udemy, Skillshare, Pluralsight, and more) across 45+ categories — including programming, web development, AI/ML, cybersecurity, design, and more. No signup required.

It helps learners compare tutorials side-by-side by rating, price, and reviews before committing to a course, which I think makes it a useful addition to this list.

- [TutorialSearch](https://tutorialsearch.io/browse/ai-machine-learning/ai-video-creation) - Free cross-platform search engine indexing 50,000+ tutorials from Udemy, Skillshare, Pluralsight, and other major learning platforms across 45+ categories.

docs: add a compilation license so GitHub is not license=none
body:
GitHub currently reports license=null for this repo: there is no LICENSE file, and README/NOTES never name one. CONTRIBUTING/NOTES already describe the list as public-domain bookmarks with a professor-takedown path; they do not say what license covers *this markdown*.

This PR only adds a compilation license for the list text (not for the linked lecture videos/universities). Defaulting to CC0-1.0 matches NOTES ("links taken from public domain websites") and other awesome-style course lists. Switch to CC-BY-4.0 if you want attribution required.

Changes:
- Add `LICENSE` (CC0-1.0) covering the repository markdown.
- One-line pointer in README Introduction and NOTES so GitHub + humans agree.

Happy to drop the files or change SPDX if you prefer to keep license unspecified.
